what: Most owners stall because they start with the hardest thing they saw online: agents, five apps at once, coding. Then they quit in a week. This is the opposite: one tool, Claude, learned in order, each step built on the one before.
One step a week. Week 1 writing, week 2 your business, week 3 files, week 4 your tools, week 5 Claude Code, week 6 a full job handed off. An hour a day is enough. Every source linked here is free.
prereqs: A Claude account. Steps 1 to 4 work on the Free plan
Claude Pro or higher for step 5 (Claude Code needs a paid plan)
A Gmail and Google Calendar account for step 4
One hour a day for 6 weeks
warn: Skip these for now: comparing 20 AI tools, adding more apps before Claude has done the job once, and courses that cost more than a month of Claude Pro. And don't jump to step 6 first. That's where most people start, and quit.

steps.h: Use Claude for your real writing
steps.p: Week 1. Emails, proposals, replies to customers. Only real work, no test prompts. Paste what you'd normally write and ask Claude to draft it or tighten it. Free source: the Claude 101 course on Claude Academy, academy.claude.com

Week 2. Go to claude.ai/projects, click + New Project and name it after your business. Click Set project instructions and paste prompt 2. Then use the + button to add your offer, your prices, 5 emails you've sent and your FAQ. Now every chat in that project starts from your business, not from zero. Free accounts get up to 5 projects. Free source: support.claude.com/en/articles/9519177

steps.h: Ask for the file, not the answer
steps.p: Week 3. Stop copying replies into Word. Turn on file creation in Settings, Capabilities (newer layouts call it Create and edit files), then ask for the file itself: the proposal as a Word doc, the price list as an Excel sheet, the pitch as a PowerPoint, the invoice as a PDF. It works on every Claude plan, Free included. Free source: support.claude.com/en/articles/12111783

Week 4. In a chat, click +, hover over Connectors and switch on Gmail and Google Calendar, then sign in with your Google account. Claude can search your email, draft replies and check your calendar. By default it asks before it sends anything. Then ask it what's waiting on you this week. Free source: support.claude.com/en/articles/10166901

Week 5. This is where it stops being a chat and starts building. Install it with the command below (Mac or Linux), or open the Claude desktop app and click the Code tab. It needs a paid plan. Ask it for one simple thing: a page, a tracker, a dashboard from your sales sheet. Free sources: code.claude.com/docs and the Claude Code 101 course on academy.claude.com
steps.code:
curl -fsSL https://claude.ai/install.sh | bash
cd your-project-folder
claude

steps.p: Week 6. Claude Code plus your connected tools can run a whole job end to end: the weekly report as a finished file, the follow-ups drafted, the lead list cleaned. Pick the job you do every week, run prompt 6, and check the result before anything goes out. Free source: code.claude.com/docs/en/quickstart

prompts.code:
Here's an email I need to send: [paste your draft, or describe it in 2 lines].
Rewrite it so it's short, direct and sounds like me, not like a template.
Give me 2 subject lines to choose from.

You work for [business name]. We sell [offer] to [who buys] at [prices].
Write like the emails in this project's files: [3 words for your tone].
If a question needs a fact that isn't in the files, ask me instead of guessing.

Make a proposal as a Word document for [client name]: scope [3 bullet points], price [amount], timeline [weeks].
Use our offer and prices from this project.
Then make our price list as an Excel sheet.

Look at my Gmail and Google Calendar for this week.
List the emails that still need a reply from me and the meetings I need to prepare for.
Draft replies for the top 3, but don't send anything.

Here's my sales sheet: [file name].csv.
Build me a one-page dashboard in a single index.html: revenue by week, top 5 products, this month vs last month.
Tell me how to open it.

Every Monday I make [the job, e.g. the weekly report] from [where the data lives].
Do it end to end and give me the finished file as [Excel or PDF] with [the sections I need].
Write the steps you took in a file called job-steps.md so we can run it the same way next week.

credit: Claude Academy free courses: Claude 101 and Claude Code 101 (academy.claude.com)
Claude Help Center: Projects (support.claude.com/en/articles/9519177)
Claude Help Center: Create and edit files with Claude (support.claude.com/en/articles/12111783)
Claude Help Center: Use Google Workspace connectors (support.claude.com/en/articles/10166901)
Claude Code docs: overview and quickstart (code.claude.com/docs)
payoff: Start step 1 today with one real email. One step a week, and in 6 weeks Claude is doing a full job for you.

ar.title: تعلّم Claude بهذا الترتيب، ساعة واحدة يوميًا.
ar.lead: لو كنت أدير عملًا يحقق 8 آلاف دولار شهريًا ولديّ ساعة واحدة يوميًا، لتعلّمت أداة واحدة هي Claude، في 6 خطوات. خطوة كل أسبوع، ومصدر مجاني لكل خطوة، وأمر واحد لكل خطوة لتبدأ به.
ar.inside: اكتب مع Claude، وأعطه تفاصيل عملك في Project، واطلب منه ملفات حقيقية، واربط Gmail وCalendar، وابنِ أول شيء لك في Claude Code، ثم سلّمه عملًا كاملًا.
what: يتوقف معظم أصحاب الأعمال لأنهم يبدؤون بأصعب ما رأوه على الإنترنت: الوكلاء، وخمسة تطبيقات دفعة واحدة، والبرمجة. ثم يستسلمون خلال أسبوع. هذا الدليل عكس ذلك: أداة واحدة هي Claude، تتعلّمها بالترتيب، وكل خطوة مبنية على التي قبلها.
خطوة واحدة كل أسبوع. الأسبوع الأول الكتابة، والثاني عملك، والثالث الملفات، والرابع أدواتك، والخامس Claude Code، والسادس تسليم عمل كامل. ساعة يوميًا تكفي. كل مصدر مذكور هنا مجاني.
prereqs: حساب Claude. الخطوات من 1 إلى 4 تعمل على الخطة المجانية
Claude Pro أو أعلى للخطوة 5 (يحتاج Claude Code إلى خطة مدفوعة)
حساب Gmail وGoogle Calendar للخطوة 4
ساعة يوميًا لمدة 6 أسابيع
ar.warn: تجاهل هذه الأمور الآن: المقارنة بين 20 أداة ذكاء اصطناعي، وإضافة تطبيقات أكثر قبل أن ينجز Claude العمل مرة واحدة، والدورات التي تكلّف أكثر من شهر من Claude Pro. ولا تقفز إلى الخطوة 6 أولًا، فمن هناك يبدأ معظم الناس ثم يستسلمون.

steps.p: الأسبوع 1. الرسائل والعروض والردود على العملاء. عمل حقيقي فقط، بلا أوامر تجريبية. الصق ما كنت ستكتبه عادة واطلب من Claude أن يكتب المسودة أو يختصرها. مصدر مجاني: دورة Claude 101 على Claude Academy، academy.claude.com

الأسبوع 2. ادخل إلى claude.ai/projects واضغط + New Project وسمّه باسم عملك. اضغط Set project instructions والصق الأمر 2. ثم استخدم زر + لإضافة عرضك وأسعارك و5 رسائل أرسلتها والأسئلة الشائعة. الآن تبدأ كل محادثة في هذا المشروع من عملك، لا من الصفر. الحسابات المجانية تحصل على 5 مشاريع كحد أقصى. مصدر مجاني: support.claude.com/en/articles/9519177

الأسبوع 3. توقّف عن نسخ الردود إلى Word. فعّل إنشاء الملفات من Settings ثم Capabilities (في الواجهات الأحدث اسمها Create and edit files)، ثم اطلب الملف نفسه: العرض كملف Word، وقائمة الأسعار كجدول Excel، والعرض التقديمي كملف PowerPoint، والفاتورة كملف PDF. يعمل ذلك على كل خطط Claude بما فيها المجانية. مصدر مجاني: support.claude.com/en/articles/12111783

الأسبوع 4. في أي محادثة اضغط + ومرّر المؤشر فوق Connectors وفعّل Gmail وGoogle Calendar، ثم سجّل الدخول بحساب Google. يستطيع Claude البحث في بريدك وكتابة مسودات الردود ومراجعة تقويمك، ويطلب موافقتك قبل إرسال أي شيء افتراضيًا. ثم اسأله عمّا ينتظرك هذا الأسبوع. مصدر مجاني: support.claude.com/en/articles/10166901

الأسبوع 5. هنا يتوقف عن كونه محادثة ويبدأ في البناء. ثبّته بالأمر أدناه (Mac أو Linux)، أو افتح تطبيق Claude على سطح المكتب واضغط تبويب Code. يحتاج إلى خطة مدفوعة. اطلب منه شيئًا واحدًا بسيطًا: صفحة، أو متتبّعًا، أو لوحة متابعة من جدول مبيعاتك. مصادر مجانية: code.claude.com/docs ودورة Claude Code 101 على academy.claude.com

الأسبوع 6. يستطيع Claude Code مع أدواتك المتصلة أن ينجز عملًا كاملًا من البداية إلى النهاية: التقرير الأسبوعي كملف جاهز، ومسودات المتابعة، وقائمة العملاء المحتملين بعد تنظيفها. اختر العمل الذي تكرره كل أسبوع، وشغّل الأمر 6، وراجع النتيجة قبل أن يخرج أي شيء. مصدر مجاني: code.claude.com/docs/en/quickstart

title: Run your AI stack like a 12-person admin team.
lead: 12 public tools, 5 departments, one job title each. Claude sits on top as chief of staff. This page gives you the org chart, a one-line job description per tool and the order to set them up.
inside: See the full org chart, know what each of the 12 tools is hired to do, pick your first hire and set the team up in an order that works.
what: Most owners collect AI tools like apps: sign up, play for a day, forget, keep paying. This guide treats each tool like a hire. One tool, one job. If you can't write the job title, you don't need the tool.

It's for owners who already use Claude or ChatGPT for basic questions and want the rest of the business to run on the same logic. Every tool here is a public product you can sign up for today. You don't need all 12. You need the one for the job you hate doing most.
prereqs: A Claude account. The Gmail and Google Calendar connectors work on every plan, Claude Code needs a paid plan (Pro or above)
A Google account with Gmail and Google Calendar
An Instagram business or creator account if you hire ManyChat
A list of the 3 jobs that eat most of your week
Check each tool's own pricing page before you sign up. Prices and free plans change
warn: Every hire is a subscription and a login that can see your data. The Gmail connector can send, reply and forward, not only draft, so keep the default where Claude asks for your approval before each one. ManyChat and Instantly send messages in your name: test every flow on yourself before it touches a real lead. And don't hire the next tool until the last one runs without you.

steps.p: One chief of staff, 5 departments, 12 tools. Claude is the one you talk to. The other 11 do the work and report back.
steps.code:
CHIEF OF STAFF
  Claude

FRONT DESK     Gmail, Google Calendar
SALES          GoHighLevel, Instantly
MARKETING      ManyChat, Higgsfield
OPERATIONS     Airtable, n8n, Claude Code
RECORDS        Fireflies, Loom

steps.h: Job descriptions: the top and the front desk
steps.p: Gmail and Calendar don't need a new subscription. You connect them inside Claude, so Claude does the reading and drafting.
steps.code:
Claude, Chief of Staff:
  drafts, plans and reads what the other 11 produce.

Gmail, Inbox Manager:
  Claude searches it through the connector and drafts replies.

Google Calendar, Scheduler:
  Claude finds free time and creates the events.

steps.p: These four touch your leads directly. Each one gets one job and nothing else.
steps.code:
GoHighLevel, Pipeline Manager:
  every lead, every stage, every follow-up in one CRM.

Instantly, Outbound Rep:
  warms up your inboxes and sends the cold email.

ManyChat, DM Receptionist:
  answers keyword comments on Instagram with a DM.

Higgsfield, Photographer:
  product shots and post images without a shoot.

steps.p: Operations is where the team talks to itself. Records is what stops you explaining the same thing twice.
steps.code:
Airtable, Office Manager:
  clients, content and orders in one base.

n8n, Operations Lead:
  moves data between every other tool.

Claude Code, In-house Builder:
  builds your dashboards and small internal tools.

Fireflies, Note Taker:
  joins the call, records it, writes the summary.

Loom, Trainer:
  records the how-to once so nobody asks twice.

steps.p: One lead, start to finish: someone comments your keyword, ManyChat sends the DM, n8n adds them to Airtable and GoHighLevel, and Claude drafts the follow-up in Gmail for you to approve. You only see the last step.

Default order, built so each hire has something to work with. If one job is bleeding money right now, jump straight to that tool, then come back to this list. Missing DMs: ManyChat. Drowning in email: Gmail with Claude. Leads going cold: GoHighLevel. Same copy-paste every day: n8n.
steps.code:
1. Claude (your chief of staff)
2. Gmail + Google Calendar connectors
3. Airtable (one base for clients and content)
4. GoHighLevel (your pipeline)
5. ManyChat (keyword DMs)
6. n8n (only once 2 tools need to talk)
7. Fireflies (call notes)
8. Loom (training videos)
9. Instantly (only once your offer converts)
10. Higgsfield (images)
11. Claude Code (dashboards on top of it all)

prompts.code:
Here are the 3 jobs that eat most of my week: [job 1], [job 2], [job 3].
My business: [what you sell, to who, roughly how many leads a week].
From this list of tools, pick ONE to set up first and tell me why:
Gmail and Google Calendar connectors, GoHighLevel, Instantly, ManyChat, Higgsfield, Airtable, n8n, Claude Code, Fireflies, Loom.
Then give me the first 5 setup steps for that one tool.

I'm hiring [tool] as my [job title].
Write its job description like a real hire:
1. The one job it owns
2. What it gets as input and from where
3. What it hands over and to who
4. How I'll know in 2 weeks it's working
5. What it is NOT allowed to do
Keep it to one page.

prompts.h: 3. Audit the team you already have
prompts.code:
Here is every AI or software tool I pay for: [tool, monthly price, what I use it for].
Give each one a job title from this org chart: Front desk, Sales, Marketing, Operations, Records.
Flag every tool with no clear job, every 2 tools doing the same job, and the job I have no tool for.
End with what to cancel and what to add, in that order.

credit: Claude, Claude Code and the Gmail and Google Calendar connectors by Anthropic (claude.com, support.claude.com)
GoHighLevel (gohighlevel.com)
Instantly (instantly.ai)
ManyChat (manychat.com)
Higgsfield (higgsfield.ai)
Airtable (airtable.com)
n8n (n8n.io)
Fireflies (fireflies.ai)
Loom (loom.com)
payoff: Hire one tool this week, the one for the job you hate most. Add the next only when the first runs without you.

ar.title: أدِر أدوات الذكاء الاصطناعي كفريق إداري من 12 شخصًا.
ar.lead: 12 أداة متاحة للجميع، و5 أقسام، ومسمى وظيفي واحد لكل أداة. يجلس Claude في القمة بصفته رئيس الموظفين. تعطيك هذه الصفحة الهيكل التنظيمي، ووصفًا وظيفيًا في سطر واحد لكل أداة، والترتيب الذي تجهّزها به.
ar.inside: اطّلع على الهيكل التنظيمي كاملًا، واعرف المهمة التي وُظّفت لها كل أداة من الأدوات الاثنتي عشرة، واختر أول تعيين لك، وجهّز الفريق بترتيب ينجح.
what: يجمع معظم أصحاب الأعمال أدوات الذكاء الاصطناعي كما يجمعون التطبيقات: يشتركون، ويجرّبون يومًا، ثم ينسون ويستمرون في الدفع. يتعامل هذا الدليل مع كل أداة كأنها موظف جديد. أداة واحدة لمهمة واحدة. إن لم تستطع كتابة مسماها الوظيفي، فأنت لا تحتاجها.

هذا الدليل لأصحاب الأعمال الذين يستخدمون Claude أو ChatGPT لأسئلة بسيطة ويريدون أن يعمل باقي عملهم بالمنطق نفسه. كل أداة هنا منتج متاح للعموم تستطيع الاشتراك فيه اليوم. لا تحتاج الأدوات الاثنتي عشرة كلها. تحتاج الأداة التي تتولى المهمة التي تكرهها أكثر من غيرها.
prereqs: حساب Claude. موصّلا Gmail وGoogle Calendar يعملان على كل الخطط، أما Claude Code فيحتاج خطة مدفوعة (Pro أو أعلى)
حساب Google فيه Gmail وGoogle Calendar
حساب Instagram تجاري أو حساب صانع محتوى إن وظّفت ManyChat
قائمة بالمهام الثلاث التي تستهلك معظم أسبوعك
راجع صفحة الأسعار الخاصة بكل أداة قبل الاشتراك. الأسعار والخطط المجانية تتغيّر
ar.warn: كل تعيين هو اشتراك وحساب دخول يستطيع رؤية بياناتك. يستطيع موصّل Gmail الإرسال والرد وإعادة التوجيه، لا كتابة المسودات فقط، لذا أبقِ الإعداد الافتراضي الذي يطلب فيه Claude موافقتك قبل كل إجراء. يرسل ManyChat وInstantly رسائل باسمك: جرّب كل مسار على نفسك قبل أن يصل إلى عميل حقيقي. ولا توظّف الأداة التالية قبل أن تعمل الأداة السابقة من دونك.

steps.p: رئيس موظفين واحد، و5 أقسام، و12 أداة. Claude هو من تتحدث إليه. الأدوات الإحدى عشرة الأخرى تنجز العمل وترفع إليه النتائج.
لا يحتاج Gmail وCalendar إلى اشتراك جديد. تربطهما داخل Claude، فيتولى Claude القراءة وكتابة المسودات.
هذه الأدوات الأربع تتعامل مع عملائك المحتملين مباشرة. كل واحدة منها تأخذ مهمة واحدة ولا شيء غيرها.
قسم العمليات هو المكان الذي يتواصل فيه الفريق مع نفسه. وقسم السجلات هو ما يمنعك من شرح الأمر نفسه مرتين.

عميل محتمل واحد من البداية إلى النهاية: يكتب أحدهم الكلمة المفتاحية في التعليقات، فيرسل ManyChat الرسالة الخاصة، ويضيفه n8n إلى Airtable وGoHighLevel، ثم يكتب Claude مسودة المتابعة في Gmail لتوافق عليها. أنت لا ترى إلا الخطوة الأخيرة.

هذا هو الترتيب الافتراضي، وهو مبني بحيث يجد كل تعيين ما يعمل عليه. إن كانت هناك مهمة تستنزف المال الآن، فابدأ مباشرة بأداتها ثم عُد إلى هذه القائمة. رسائل خاصة تضيع: ManyChat. بريد يغرقك: Gmail مع Claude. عملاء يبردون: GoHighLevel. نسخ ولصق متكرر كل يوم: n8n.

title: Fable 5.2 vs Opus 5.5: the bill.
lead: Same 7 builds, same prompts, first try in Claude Code. Opus 5.5 cost $16.37. Fable 5.2 cost $39.29. Here's the full bill, 7 build prompts to rerun it, the two-command setup that ran all 7 for $25.81, and how to test it on your own work.
inside: Read the cost of every run, get 7 build prompts, set up Opus as the builder with Fable as the advisor, run one build on the first try, then run it on Fable alone and compare the bill.
what: Charlie Hills gave Claude's two top models the same 7 build prompts in Claude Code on Nov 10, 2026. One shot each, no fixes. Every prompt asked for a single self-contained HTML file built with Three.js: a black hole, robot arms solving a Rubik's cube, a 3D shooter, a smart speaker, a product configurator, a sales globe and a retro shooter. Fable's versions looked richer on almost every one. On the one build that needed real logic, the Rubik's cube, only Opus wrote a real solver.

The gap comes from two places. Per token, Fable 5.2 costs twice what Opus 5.5 does on the API ($8 in and $40 out per million tokens, against $4 and $20). And on the 4 builds Charlie timed, Fable also ran longer. His fix is to run both: Opus builds, Fable checks the hard parts. That setup ran all 7 for $25.81.
prereqs: Claude Code v2.1.321 or later (Fable 5.2 needs it)

Fable access. Max, Ultra and Team or Enterprise premium seats use plan limits, capped at 50% of the weekly limit. Pro and standard seats bill Fable to usage credits, except Pro's launch window, which ends Nov 16, 2026 at 11:59 pm PT
Claude Code signed in through Anthropic directly (a Claude plan or an API key). The advisor doesn't run on Amazon Bedrock, Google Cloud or Microsoft Foundry
One build prompt to test with: one of Charlie's 7, or a real job from your business
warn: These numbers are one run per build, from one person, priced at API rates. Your bill will be different, so treat it as a direction, not a quote. On a plan, Fable eats your weekly limit faster than other models, and on Pro after Nov 16 it bills usage credits. In non-interactive mode (claude -p) Claude Code bills those credits without asking. Check /usage after every run.

steps.p: Fable 5.2 needs Claude Code v2.1.321 or later. Update, then check the version before you start.

Charlie's numbers, one shot each, no fixes. Build times were published for the first 4 builds only. His exact prompts aren't public, so prompts 1 to 7 in this guide are our own versions of the same 7 builds. Your bill will land close to his, not on the cent.
steps.code:
Build                 Opus 5.5        Fable 5.2        Gap
Black hole            $0.92  5.1 min  $2.78  8.2 min   3.0x
Robot arms            $2.88 16.7 min  $7.25 27.7 min   2.5x
3D shooter            $2.31 12.4 min  $5.32 14.8 min   2.3x
Smart speaker         $2.33 13.3 min  $4.51 13.6 min   1.9x
Product configurator  $3.28           $6.60            2.0x
Sales globe           $1.15           $3.40            3.0x
Retro shooter         $3.50           $9.43            2.7x
All 7 builds          $16.37          $39.29           2.4x

Opus builds, Fable advises: $25.81 for all 7

steps.p: Open Claude Code in an empty folder and set Opus 5.5 as the main model. Opus does the building.

steps.h: Turn on Fable as the advisor
steps.p: Claude now calls Fable at the hard moments: before it picks an approach, when an error keeps coming back, and before it says it's done. You'll see an Advising line when it does. If Claude Code points you to /model fable instead, your plan needs a one-time OK to bill Fable to usage credits: accept it there, switch back with /model opus, then run /advisor fable again.

steps.h: Paste one prompt, take the first try
steps.p: Paste one of prompts 1 to 7 once and let it finish. No fixes, no follow-ups, or the comparison means nothing. When it's done, open the file it built, then run /usage and write down what the session used.

steps.h: Run it on Fable alone and compare
steps.p: Turn the advisor off, start a fresh session in a new folder, switch to Fable and paste the exact same prompt. First try again. Put both results side by side and compare the build and the bill. Then decide which jobs earn Fable and which ones Opus handles fine.

Colour swatches and 3 materials change the model live, the price updates with each option, and I can rotate it with the mouse.
Put everything in one index.html I can open in the browser, no build step.

prompts.h: 9. Turn a real job into a test
prompts.code:
Here's a task I do in my business every week: [describe it].
Turn it into one prompt I can paste into Claude Code and run once, with no fixes, on two different models.
Spell out exactly what done looks like, so I can judge both results the same way.

Advisor setup from the Claude Code docs (code.claude.com/docs/en/advisor)
Fable plan rules from Anthropic's Help Center: Claude Fable models on your plan (support.claude.com)
payoff: Run one build on Opus with Fable advising this week, then the same prompt on Fable alone. Your own bill tells you more than anyone's test.

ar.title: Fable 5.2 مقابل Opus 5.5: الفاتورة.
ar.lead: سبعة مشاريع بناء، الأوامر نفسها، المحاولة الأولى في Claude Code. كلّف Opus 5.5 مبلغ 16.37 دولارًا، وكلّف Fable 5.2 مبلغ 39.29 دولارًا. في هذا الدليل الفاتورة كاملة، و7 أوامر بناء لتكرار الاختبار، والإعداد بأمرين الذي نفّذ المشاريع السبعة بـ 25.81 دولارًا، وطريقة اختباره على عملك أنت.
ar.inside: اطّلع على تكلفة كل تشغيل، وخذ 7 أوامر بناء، واجعل Opus يبني وFable يعمل مستشارًا، ونفّذ مشروعًا واحدًا من المحاولة الأولى، ثم نفّذه على Fable وحده وقارن الفاتورتين.
what: أعطى Charlie Hills أقوى نموذجين لدى Claude الأوامر السبعة نفسها في Claude Code بتاريخ 10 نوفمبر 2026، محاولة واحدة لكلٍّ منها بلا أي تصحيح. طلب كل أمر ملف HTML واحدًا مستقلًا مبنيًا بـ Three.js: ثقب أسود، وذراعان آليتان تحلّان مكعب روبيك، ولعبة تصويب ثلاثية الأبعاد، ومكبّر صوت ذكي، وأداة لتخصيص منتج، وكرة أرضية للمبيعات، ولعبة تصويب بطابع قديم. بدت نسخ Fable أغنى في كل المشاريع تقريبًا. وفي المشروع الوحيد الذي احتاج منطقًا حقيقيًا، مكعب روبيك، كان Opus الوحيد الذي كتب حلًّا فعليًا.

يأتي الفرق من مصدرين. سعر Fable 5.2 لكل رمز (token) ضعف سعر Opus 5.5 عبر API: ثمانية دولارات للإدخال وأربعون للإخراج لكل مليون رمز، مقابل أربعة دولارات للإدخال وعشرين للإخراج لدى Opus. وفي المشاريع الأربعة التي قاس Charlie وقتها، استغرق Fable وقتًا أطول أيضًا. والحل الذي يقترحه هو تشغيل الاثنين معًا: Opus يبني وFable يراجع الأجزاء الصعبة. نفّذ هذا الإعداد المشاريع السبعة بـ 25.81 دولارًا.
prereqs: Claude Code بالإصدار v2.1.321 أو أحدث (يحتاجه Fable 5.2)

إمكانية استخدام Fable. خطط Max وUltra والمقاعد المميزة في Team وEnterprise تستخدم حدود الخطة بسقف 50% من الحد الأسبوعي. أما Pro والمقاعد العادية فتحتسب Fable من رصيد الاستخدام الإضافي، باستثناء فترة إطلاق Pro التي تنتهي في 16 نوفمبر 2026 الساعة 11:59 مساءً بتوقيت المحيط الهادئ
Claude Code مسجّل الدخول عبر Anthropic مباشرة (خطة Claude أو مفتاح API). لا يعمل المستشار على Amazon Bedrock أو Google Cloud أو Microsoft Foundry
أمر بناء واحد للاختبار: أحد أوامر Charlie السبعة، أو مهمة حقيقية من عملك
ar.warn: هذه الأرقام من تشغيل واحد لكل مشروع، ومن شخص واحد، ومحسوبة بأسعار API. فاتورتك ستختلف، فاعتبرها مؤشرًا لا عرض سعر. على الخطط، يستهلك Fable حدّك الأسبوعي أسرع من النماذج الأخرى، وعلى Pro بعد 16 نوفمبر يُحتسب من رصيد الاستخدام الإضافي. وفي الوضع غير التفاعلي (claude -p) يحتسب Claude Code هذا الرصيد دون أن يسألك. راجع /usage بعد كل تشغيل.

steps.p: يحتاج Fable 5.2 إلى Claude Code بالإصدار v2.1.321 أو أحدث. حدّثه، ثم تحقق من الإصدار قبل أن تبدأ.

أرقام Charlie، محاولة واحدة لكل مشروع بلا تصحيح. نُشرت أوقات البناء لأول أربعة مشاريع فقط. أوامره الأصلية غير منشورة، لذلك الأوامر من 1 إلى 7 في هذا الدليل نسخنا الخاصة من المشاريع السبعة نفسها. ستقترب فاتورتك من فاتورته، لكنها لن تطابقها بالسنت.
افتح Claude Code في مجلد فارغ واجعل Opus 5.5 النموذج الرئيسي. Opus هو من يبني.

سيستدعي Claude الآن Fable في اللحظات الصعبة: قبل أن يختار طريقة العمل، وعندما يتكرر خطأ ما، وقبل أن يعلن انتهاءه. سترى سطر Advising عندما يحدث ذلك. إذا وجّهك Claude Code إلى /model fable بدلًا من ذلك، فخطتك تحتاج موافقة لمرة واحدة على احتساب Fable من رصيد الاستخدام الإضافي: وافق هناك، ثم عُد بـ /model opus، ثم شغّل /advisor fable مرة أخرى.

steps.h: الصق أمرًا واحدًا وخذ المحاولة الأولى
steps.p: الصق أحد الأوامر من 1 إلى 7 مرة واحدة واتركه حتى ينتهي. لا تصحيح ولا أسئلة متابعة، وإلا تفقد المقارنة معناها. عندما ينتهي، افتح الملف الذي بناه، ثم شغّل /usage وسجّل ما استهلكته الجلسة.

أوقف المستشار، وابدأ جلسة جديدة في مجلد جديد، وانتقل إلى Fable، والصق الأمر نفسه تمامًا. المحاولة الأولى مجددًا. ضع النتيجتين جنبًا إلى جنب وقارن البناء والفاتورة. ثم قرّر أي المهام تستحق Fable وأيها يكفيها Opus.

title: 18 jobs Claude can do in your business.
lead: Six departments, three jobs each, and the exact line to type for every one. Seventeen run in the normal Claude app. One needs Claude Code.
inside: Switch on the 3 features the map needs, then run the 18 copy-paste prompts: sales, marketing, admin, money, customers and reporting.
what: Most owners use Claude for one thing: rewriting an email. The map shows the rest. Every job on it uses a feature Anthropic lists on its own help pages: web search, file creation (Word, Excel, PDF), Projects, and the Gmail, Calendar and Drive connectors.
Don't run all 18 this week. Pick the department that eats most of your week, run its 3 jobs every day for 7 days, and only then move to the next one. That's how a job becomes a habit and not a demo.
prereqs: A Claude account. File creation, Projects and the Google connectors are on every plan, Free included
Claude on the web or the Claude Desktop app
Your Gmail, Google Calendar and Google Drive (for the admin and customer jobs)
A paid plan only for job 18 (the dashboard), which runs in Claude Code
warn: Claude asks before it sends an email by default. Keep that on. Read every proposal, reply and figure before it reaches a customer: Claude can misread a PDF or a number. On a Team or Enterprise plan, the owner has to switch on web search, file creation and the connectors for the workspace first (Organization settings).

steps.p: In Claude, open Settings, then Capabilities, and switch on Code execution and file creation (in the newer layout it's called Create and edit files). This is what lets Claude hand you a Word doc, an Excel sheet or a PDF. Files can be up to 30MB each.

In a chat, click the + button, hover over Connectors and switch on Gmail, Google Calendar and Google Drive. The first time, Claude asks you to sign in with your Google account. You can switch each one off from the same menu.

steps.h: Switch on web search when you need it
steps.p: For jobs 1 and 6, click + in the chat and pick Web search. A checkmark shows it's on. Claude then reads live pages and gives you the links it used.

Go to claude.ai/projects, click + New Project and name it (Sales, Marketing). Click Set project instructions and paste 3 lines about your business: what you sell, who buys, how you talk. Add your price list and a few past emails to the project knowledge. Free plans can have 5 projects.
Choose the department that takes most of your week. Run its 3 prompts from the next pages every day for 7 days. When they feel normal, move to the next branch.

prompts.code: Search the web for [company name] in [city]. Tell me what they sell, who runs it, any news from the last 6 months and 3 questions I should ask on our call. List your sources.

prompts.h: Sales 2. Proposal as a Word doc
prompts.code:
Here are my call notes:
[paste notes]

Turn them into a proposal as a Word doc. Use only the prices in my price list. Flag anything I didn't price.
Find my last email thread with [client name] in Gmail and draft a follow-up that confirms what we agreed and the next step. Save it as a draft. Don't send it.
Using the examples in this project, write 3 LinkedIn posts about [topic]. One idea each, short lines, no hashtags.

Here are [20] customer reviews:
[paste reviews]

Pull the phrases customers repeat and write 5 ad headlines in their words.
Search the web for what [competitor 1], [competitor 2] and [competitor 3] posted or announced this week. One line each, with the link.

prompts.h: Admin 7. Find a slot and book it
prompts.code: Find a free 30-minute slot next week when I and [name, email] are both available, then create the event called [title]. Show me the slot before you book it.
Search my Google Drive for the [file you need, e.g. supplier contract from March]. Give me the file name, the link and when it was last changed.

Here are my notes on how I [task]:
[paste notes]

Turn them into numbered steps a new hire can follow without asking me.
I'm uploading [8] invoice PDFs. Put them in one Excel sheet: supplier, invoice number, date, amount, due date. Add a total at the bottom.

prompts.h: Money 11. Sales chart from a CSV
prompts.code: Here's my sales export as a CSV. Chart sales by week for the last 3 months and tell me in 3 lines what changed.

Here's my price list:
[paste or upload it]

Turn it into an Excel sheet: item, price, unit, notes. One row per item.

prompts.h: Customers 13. FAQ answers from your files
prompts.code: Using only the files in this project, answer this customer question: [paste question]. If the answer isn't in the files, say so.
Find the unanswered customer emails in my Gmail from the last 3 days and draft a reply to each. Save them as drafts. Don't send anything.

Here are my reviews as a CSV:
[upload file]

Group the complaints, count each group and list the top 5 with one real quote each.

prompts.h: Reporting 16. Weekly report as a PDF
prompts.code: Here are this week's sales and leads exports. Build a one-page weekly report as a PDF: totals, change from last week, and 3 things to fix.
Check my Gmail and Google Calendar. List what's waiting on me this week: emails I haven't answered, meetings with no prep and anything due.
Build a one-page sales dashboard from sales.csv in this folder. Show sales by week, top 5 products and new vs repeat customers. Make it an HTML file I can open in my browser.

credit: Features from Anthropic's Help Center (support.claude.com): file creation, Projects, web search and the Google Workspace connectors. Claude Code from code.claude.com
Map and prompts written by Karem AlMoayyad for Karemops.ai
payoff: Pick your heaviest department tonight. Run its 3 jobs tomorrow morning, before you open your inbox.

title: Write down how your business runs. Then add AI.
lead: Claude follows what you give it. Give it a messy process and you get the same mess, faster. This is the one-page process doc to write first.
inside: List the jobs you repeat, write 3 lines for each, fill in the one-page template, and let Claude find the gaps before you hand anything off.
what: Most owners want the automation first: the follow-ups, the reports, the DM replies. Then it breaks on day 2, because nobody wrote down what the job is. Claude can't guess what's in your head, and neither can a new hire.

The fix is boring and it works. For every job you repeat, write what comes in, what you do with it and what goes out. The jobs you can write cleanly are the ones to hand off first, to Claude or to a person.
prereqs: A notes app or a Google Doc
30 minutes for your first 10 jobs
A Claude account (any plan) for the gap check in step 4
Optional: a voice memo app, if talking is easier than typing
warn: Don't automate a job you haven't run by hand from the doc at least once. If you skip a step when you follow your own doc, the doc is wrong. Fix it before Claude or anyone else uses it.

steps.p: Go through last week: your sent emails, your DMs, your calendar. Write every job you did more than once. Answering price questions, sending invoices, booking calls, posting. Aim for 10 to 20.
What comes in (a DM, an invoice, a form). What you do with it. What goes out (a reply, a file, a booking). If you can't write the 3 lines, the job isn't clear yet. Mark it and move on.
steps.code:
Job: [name]
Comes in: [what arrives, and where]
I do: [the steps, in order]
Goes out: [what leaves, and to whom]

steps.p: For the 3 jobs that cost you the most time, fill in the full template below. One page each. Use your real tools by name: Gmail, Airtable, GoHighLevel, WhatsApp.
steps.code:
JOB: [name]
OWNER: [who does it today]
TRIGGER: [what starts it]
INPUT: [what arrives and where]
STEPS:
1. [first thing you do]
2. [next]
3. [next]
OUTPUT: [what leaves, to whom]
TOOLS: [apps you touch]
RULES: [prices, limits, what you never do]
DONE WHEN: [how you know it's finished]
WHEN IT GOES WRONG: [the usual problem and the fix]

steps.p: Paste one filled doc into Claude with the first prompt on the next page. It asks the questions a new hire would ask. Answer them in the doc, not in the chat.
Rank your jobs with the last prompt. Hand off the one with the clearest doc first. Run it from the doc for a week, fix what breaks, then pick the next.

prompts.code:
Here's how I do [job]:
[paste the doc]

You're a new hire doing this for the first time. List every question you'd have to ask me before you could do it alone.

Here's a transcript of me explaining how I [job]:
[paste transcript]

Turn it into this template: JOB, TRIGGER, INPUT, STEPS, OUTPUT, TOOLS, RULES, DONE WHEN. Leave a field empty if I didn't say it.
Interview me about how I [job]. Ask one question at a time. When you have enough, write the one-page process doc.

Here are my process docs:
[paste them]

Rank them by how clearly they're written and how often the job happens. Tell me which one to hand off first, and why.

credit: Process doc template and prompts written by Karem AlMoayyad for Karemops.ai
payoff: Tonight, write the 3 lines for 10 jobs. Tomorrow, hand off the cleanest one.

title: 10 giveaways that tell clients AI wrote it.
lead: The checklist to run before you hit send, with the fix for each one, plus the prompt that checks your draft for you.
inside: The 10 giveaways with a before and after for each, then 3 prompts: check a draft, fix it, and stop the giveaways at the source.
what: Readers have seen enough AI text to spot it. One giveaway is fine. Three in one email and the reader stops trusting the rest, including your price.

Most of these are habits AI models fall into: long dashes, "it's not just X, it's Y", lists of three, words like "delve". Delete them and the email reads like a person wrote it, because a person checked it.
prereqs: The email, post or proposal you're about to send
Any Claude plan for the check prompts
2 minutes per email
warn: This list catches patterns, not facts. A clean-sounding email can still have a wrong price or name. Read it for facts after you fix the style.

steps.p: Delete the long dash (the one between two words, like this example: fast—cheap). Use a period or a comma. "We ship fast. Most orders land in 2 days."
Say the real thing. Not "It's not just a tool, it's a partner" but "It answers your DMs at night."
Lists of three for rhythm ("fast, simple and powerful") sound written by a machine. Two is fine. One real detail is better.
Swap for plain words: "look at", "smooth", "use". Same for "robust", "pivotal", "showcase" and "foster".
Delete the warm-up. Start with the point: "Here's the quote for the April job."
Answer the question. Praise before an answer reads as filler, and clients notice.
Fake-candid openers. Just say it: "The deadline won't work. Can we do the 14th?"
Write the actual claim. "At its core, our service is about trust" becomes "We answer within 2 hours."
Use "is" and "has". "The office boasts parking" becomes "The office has parking."

steps.h: 10. "In order to", "due to the fact that"
steps.p: Use "to" and "because". Shorter, and it sounds like you talking.

prompts.code:
Check this email for these AI giveaways: long dashes mid-sentence, "it's not just X, it's Y", lists of three, words like delve, seamless, leverage, robust, "let's dive in", "great question", "honestly?", "here's the thing", "at its core", "serves as", "boasts", "in order to", "due to the fact that".
Quote each one you find and give the fix. Don't rewrite the rest.

[paste email]

Rewrite this email with those giveaways removed. Keep my words where they're fine, keep it the same length or shorter, and don't add anything I didn't say.

[paste email]

Add this to your project instructions:
Never use long dashes. Never write "it's not just X, it's Y". Don't list three things for rhythm. Never use: delve, seamless, leverage, robust, pivotal, showcase, foster. No warm-up openers, no praise before answers. Use "is" and "has", not "serves as" or "boasts".

credit: Checklist and prompts written by Karem AlMoayyad for Karemops.ai, from common patterns in AI-written text
payoff: Before your next send, run prompt 1 on it. Then put prompt 3 in your project so the next draft comes out clean.

title: 3 AI systems I'd install in an $8K/mo business.
lead: Content, ads and numbers. What each system does, what goes into it, what it needs from you, and which one to build first.
inside: How the Content System, the Ad System and the numbers dashboard work, the stack behind each (Airtable, Claude Code, N8N, Supabase), and a starter prompt for each.
what: Most owners buy AI tools one at a time and none of them talk to each other. A system is different: ideas go in one end, finished work comes out the other, and the same place holds every step. Your team still runs it. The system decides what to make and drafts it, so nobody starts from a blank page.
All three are built with Claude Code. Start with the one that matches your biggest leak: no content going out, ads you can't read, or numbers you only see at the end of the month.
prereqs: Claude Code (paid Claude plan) to build them
An Airtable account (the free plan is enough to start)
N8N (cloud or self-hosted) to move work between steps
Access to your Meta ad account, for systems 2 and 3
One person on your team who will run it every week
warn: A system is only as good as what you feed it. If nobody approves the scripts or checks the dashboard, it stops working in 3 weeks. Pick the owner before you build. And keep a person on every ad launch: Claude drafts, a person presses publish.

steps.p: An Airtable base holds every idea, script and post. Claude Code pulls what competitors posted and turns the winners into angles. It writes scripts and carousel outlines in your voice. N8N moves each approved piece into a publishing queue. Your team films, checks and posts. Needs from you: a voice doc, 3 competitors, and 30 minutes a week to approve.

First, your Meta ad account gets cleaned up: one campaign structure, clear names, and the pixel and Conversions API checked. Then a Claude Code engine scrapes competitor ads from the Meta Ad Library, writes ad briefs from what's working, and preps launches. Needs from you: access to the ad account, your offer, and a person who makes the creatives.

One page that shows where your funnel breaks, refreshed every week. Ad spend, leads, calls and sales sit side by side, so you see which step leaks. The data lives in Supabase and the page is built with Claude Code. Needs from you: access to your ad account and wherever your leads and sales live (GoHighLevel, Airtable, Shopify).
No content going out? Build System 1. Spending on ads but can't tell what works? Build System 3, then 2. Never build all three at once. Each one needs 2 to 4 weeks of use before it runs smoothly.
Write down who runs it, what they check each week and where they flag problems. Without an owner, every system turns back into a pile of tools.

prompts.code: I'm building a content system in Airtable. Design the base: one table for ideas, one for scripts, one for posts, linked to each other. Give me every field, its type and the status values from idea to posted. Then write it as a setup checklist I can follow.

Here are [10] competitor ads from the Meta Ad Library (copy and what the visual shows):
[paste them]

Group them by angle, tell me which angles show up most, and write 3 ad briefs for my offer: [your offer]. Hook, angle, what the visual shows, call to action.

In this folder are 3 CSV exports: ads.csv, leads.csv, sales.csv. Build a one-page HTML dashboard: spend, leads, cost per lead, calls, sales, by week. Highlight the step where the drop is biggest. Tell me which columns you matched between files.

credit: Systems and prompts by Karem AlMoayyad for Karemops.ai. Tools named: Claude Code (Anthropic), Airtable, N8N, Supabase, Meta Ad Library
payoff: Pick the one leak that costs you most this month. Build that system first, and give it an owner before you start.

title: Your Monday report, built by Claude.
lead: Three files you already export, one Claude Project, and one message every Monday. Here are the 9 tiles and the prompts behind them.
inside: Export 3 CSVs, set up the Project once, then send one line every Monday. Includes the full report prompt and a prompt for each of the 9 tiles.
what: Most owners build the weekly report by hand, or don't build it at all and find the problem a month late. Claude can read CSV files, analyse them and hand back a PDF or an Excel file. That's on every plan.
The setup takes one afternoon. After that it's 3 uploads and one message. The report compares this week with last week and flags anything that dropped, so you read 9 tiles instead of 3 spreadsheets.
prereqs: A Claude account with file creation switched on (Settings, then Capabilities)
Your sales export (Shopify, your POS, or an invoice sheet)
Your leads export (Airtable or GoHighLevel)
Your Meta ad spend export from Ads Manager
Optional: the Google Calendar connector, for tile 9
warn: Check the first 2 reports against your own numbers before you trust them. Claude can match the wrong column or miss a refund. Keep the column names the same every week, so it reads the files the same way.

steps.p: Sales for the last 2 weeks, leads for the last 2 weeks (in Airtable, open the view and download it as CSV; GoHighLevel exports contacts as CSV), and ad spend by day from Meta Ads Manager. Same date range in all three.
Go to claude.ai/projects, click + New Project and call it Monday Report. Click Set project instructions and paste the report prompt from the next pages. Now you never have to type it again.
Start a new chat in the project, upload the 3 CSVs and send: "Build this week's report." Claude builds the 9 tiles as a PDF and flags anything that dropped more than 10%.
If a tile is wrong (wrong column, wrong week), tell Claude in the same chat, then update the project instructions so it doesn't happen again. Do this for 2 weeks.
Export, upload, send the line. Read the flags first. If you want tile 9 (calls you haven't prepped), switch on the Google Calendar connector in the chat with + then Connectors.

prompts.code: Every week I upload 3 CSVs: sales, leads, ad spend. Build a one-page PDF report with 9 tiles: sales this week vs last week, new leads and their source, calls booked, close rate, best seller, ad spend vs sales, unpaid invoices, top customer complaint, and next week's calls I haven't prepped. Compare every number with last week. Flag anything that dropped more than 10% in red at the top. If a file is missing a column you need, say which one.
Total sales this week and last week, and the % change.
New leads this week, split by source. Which source grew most?
How many leads have a booked call this week?
Of the calls held this week, how many became sales? Show it as a %.
Top product or service by units and by revenue this week.
Ad spend this week next to sales this week. Sales per $1 spent.
List invoices still unpaid, oldest first, with the total.
From the notes or reviews column, the most common complaint this week, with a count.
Check my Google Calendar for next week. List sales calls that have no notes or agenda yet.

payoff: This Friday, export the 3 files and set up the project. Monday morning, send one line.

title: Call notes in. Proposal out. Nothing unpriced.
lead: A Claude Project that knows your prices, and one prompt that turns any call into a Word doc proposal and flags the work you forgot to price.
inside: Set up a Proposals Project with your price list and a past proposal, then run the prompt after every call. Includes 3 follow-up prompts.
what: Writing a proposal after a call takes most owners an evening. And the costly part isn't the time: it's the extra the client asked for on the call that never made it onto the price list, so you do it for free.

Claude can read your notes and your price list and write the proposal as a Word doc, on any plan. The last line of the prompt is the one that pays: it tells Claude to flag anything you didn't price, so you see it before you send.
prereqs: A Claude account with file creation switched on (Settings, then Capabilities)
Your price list (a PDF, a sheet or plain text)
One past proposal you liked
Your notes or the transcript from the call
warn: Read the flags and every price before you send. Claude uses only what's in your price list if you tell it to, but it can still misread a line. Never send a proposal you haven't read top to bottom.

steps.p: Go to claude.ai/projects and click + New Project. Name it Proposals.

steps.h: Add your price list and a past proposal
steps.p: In the project knowledge panel, click + and upload your price list and one past proposal you liked. Claude uses the first for numbers and the second for layout and tone.
Click Set project instructions and paste this. It applies to every chat in the project.
steps.code:
You write proposals for [business name].
Use only the prices in the price list file. Never invent a price, a discount or a deadline.
Follow the layout of the past proposal file.
Always end with a list called FLAGS: anything the client asked for that isn't on my price list, and anything in the notes that's unclear.

steps.p: Start a new chat in the project, paste or upload your call notes, and send the main prompt from the next page. You get a Word doc and a list of flags.
Go through the FLAGS list. Add a price, cut the item, or ask the client. Then ask Claude to update the doc and send it yourself.

prompts.code:
Turn these call notes into a proposal. Use only the prices in my price list. Word doc. Flag anything I didn't price.

[paste call notes]
Add [item] at [price] to the proposal, update the total and give me the new Word doc.
Write a short email to send with this proposal. Remind them of the one problem they told me about on the call and the next step. Under 100 words.
Read the proposal like the client would. List anything unclear, any price that doesn't match the price list, and any promise I didn't make on the call.

title: 50 Black Friday DMs. One Claude Project.
lead: Black Friday is Friday 27 November. Set this up before Thursday night and you answer in seconds instead of losing the sale to a slow reply.
inside: A Claude Project for the sale, the 10 answers written before anyone asks, Meta Business Suite FAQs and keyword replies, and a fast way to answer the rest.
what: On a sale day the same 10 questions arrive 50 times: is it on all sizes, do you ship here, when does the code end. Every slow reply is a sale that goes somewhere else.

Claude doesn't read your Instagram DMs, so the setup splits the work. Claude writes the answers from your sale details. Meta Business Suite sends the common ones by itself. For everything else, you paste the DM into Claude and send its draft.
prereqs: A Claude account (any plan; Projects are on Free too)
Your Instagram business account or Facebook Page connected to Meta Business Suite
Your Black Friday details: prices, the code, dates, shipping, returns
10 real replies you've sent customers before (for your voice)
warn: Meta's keyword replies only fire on an exact match and are case-sensitive, and they wait 15 minutes in case you reply yourself. If you've switched on Meta Business Agent, Meta pauses away messages and instant replies. Check every price and date in the answers before Friday.

steps.h: Make a Claude Project for the sale
steps.p: Go to claude.ai/projects, click + New Project and name it Black Friday. Upload one file with your sale prices, the code and when it ends, shipping, and returns. Add 10 replies you've sent before, so the answers sound like you.

steps.h: Write the answers before anyone asks
steps.p: Start a chat in the project and send prompt 1 from the next page. You get the 10 questions customers will DM most, each with a short reply in your voice. Fix any fact that's off.

steps.h: Put the top ones in Meta Business Suite
steps.p: In Business Suite, open Inbox, then automations. Use the Frequently asked questions template for the top questions, and Custom keywords (desktop only) for words like "shipping" or "code". Keywords match exactly and are case-sensitive, so add the spellings people use. Automations work across Messenger, Instagram and WhatsApp accounts you've connected.

steps.h: Paste in anything that doesn't fit
steps.p: When a DM doesn't match, copy it into the Black Friday project with prompt 2. Claude drafts the reply from your sale file. You read it and send it.

prompts.code: Using my sale file and my past replies, write the 10 questions customers will DM me most this week, and a reply to each in my voice, under 300 characters. Use only facts from the sale file.

A customer sent this:
[paste the DM]

Draft my reply from the sale file, in my voice, under 300 characters. If the answer isn't in the file, tell me what's missing.
For each of the 10 questions, list the words a customer would type in a DM, including short and misspelled versions (ship, shiping, delivery). Max 5 per question.

Here are the DMs I answered by hand today:
[paste them]

Which questions came up most that my FAQs didn't cover? Write a reply for each so I can add them for Saturday.
